question: At an unmarked junction of two equal roads, another car approaches from your right. What must you do?
optionB: Carry on, you are going straight
optionC: Flash your lights and go first
optionD: Go first if you are faster
explanation: Under the Road Traffic Act a driver gives way to a vehicle approaching from the right unless signs or another rule say otherwise. This is the right-hand rule (oikeanpuoleisen sääntö).

question: You are turning left at a junction and a car is coming straight towards you from the opposite direction. Who goes first?
optionD: You, if the road is wide
explanation: A driver turning left must give way to oncoming traffic as well as to anyone crossing the road being entered.

question: You turn left into a side road while a moped rider is crossing it on a cycle crossing. Who goes first?
explanation: A turning driver must give way to pedestrians, cyclists and moped riders crossing the road being entered.

question: You drive out of a supermarket car park onto a street. A car is coming from your left. Who gives way?
explanation: A driver coming onto a road from a car park, a yard, a fuel station or a similar area must always give way to other road users, from either side.

question: You leave a pihakatu (residential street) and enter an ordinary street. A cyclist approaches from your left. What must you do?
optionB: Go first, you are on the right
explanation: Anyone coming onto a road from a pihakatu or a kävelykatu (pedestrian street) must give way to all other road users there.

question: You drive along a forest track and reach a public road. A car approaches from your left on the road. What must you do?
optionA: Carry on, it is on your left
optionD: Go first, as you arrived first
explanation: A vehicle coming from a path or a similar minor track must give way to other road users. The right-hand rule does not help it.

question: You leave a cycle path and ride a moped onto the carriageway. Who has priority?
explanation: A vehicle moving from a cycle path onto the carriageway must give way to other traffic there unless the other road user has to give way under another rule.

question: You come out of a garage across a pavement towards the road. A child is walking along the pavement. What must you do?
explanation: Crossing a pavement or a cycle path, a driver must give way to the pedestrians, cyclists and moped riders using it.

question: You are about to leave a roundabout. A cyclist is crossing the exit road on a cycle crossing. What must you do?
explanation: A driver leaving a roundabout must give way to pedestrians, cyclists and moped riders crossing the road being entered.

question: A give-way sign stands at your approach to a roundabout. Who has priority?
optionA: You, as you come from the right
explanation: In Finland roundabout entries are normally marked with give-way signs, so you give way to traffic already on the roundabout. Signs override the right-hand rule.

question: A yellow diamond with a white border stands at the side of your road. What does it tell you?
optionA: A junction with a priority road
explanation: This sign marks a priority road (etuajo-oikeutettu tie). Traffic joining it from side roads must give way to you.

question: You drive through a village on a road signed as a priority road. Does the right-hand rule apply at its side roads?
optionD: No, side roads give way to you
explanation: Signs come before the right-hand rule. Traffic from the side roads of a priority road has a give-way or stop sign, so you keep priority, but drive with care in case someone pulls out.

question: A police car with flashing blue lights and siren approaches from behind. What should you do?
optionC: Keep going at the same speed
optionD: Stop at once in your lane
explanation: Every road user must give an emergency vehicle using its siren and blue lights a clear passage, moving aside or stopping if needed.

question: A supervised group of schoolchildren is crossing the road in a line. What may you not do?
optionA: Wait for all of them to cross
explanation: The Road Traffic Act forbids interrupting or blocking a supervised group of children or an organised procession.

question: A tram rings its bell as it nears a crossing you are about to drive onto. What should you do?
explanation: Trams must be given unobstructed passage unless the law says otherwise. Never stop on the tracks in front of a tram.

question: A bus at a stop signals to pull out. The speed limit is 50 km/h and you are in the next lane. What must you do?
explanation: Where the limit is 60 km/h or less, traffic approaching the stop in the same or the adjacent lane must give way to a bus signalling to leave.

question: A bus signals to leave a stop on a road where the limit is 80 km/h. What is the legal position?
optionA: The bus must wait for a gap
optionC: It may pull out at any time
explanation: The duty to give way to a bus leaving a stop applies only on roads with a limit of 60 km/h or less. On faster roads the bus waits, though considerate drivers help when safe.

question: How should you show that you intend to give way?
explanation: The law requires a driver who has to give way to show it clearly and in good time by reducing speed or stopping.

question: You turn left from a two-way road into another two-way road. Where should your car be once the turn is done?
optionA: In its left lane at first, then right
optionC: On the right side of the new road
explanation: After turning left you enter the right-hand side of the road you join, without cutting the corner across oncoming traffic.

question: On a one-way street with two lanes you will turn left at the next corner. Which lane should you be in?
explanation: On a one-way carriageway a vehicle turning left moves to its left edge, in the left-hand lane, in good time before the turn.

question: A lorry ahead signals right and swings out to the left before its turn. What should you avoid?
explanation: Long vehicles often move out before turning. Stay behind and never squeeze into the gap on the side it is turning towards.

question: Two oncoming cars both want to turn left at the same junction. What does the law allow?
optionA: They must pass behind each other
optionB: Turning in front of each other
optionD: Only the first to signal turns
explanation: Oncoming vehicles normally keep to the right of each other. When both turn left at a junction, they may pass on the left, turning in front of each other, with special care.

question: A traffic light shows green, but a give-way sign stands at the same junction. Which one do you follow?
explanation: Traffic lights take precedence over signs showing a duty to give way. When the lights work, follow them.

question: A snowmobile comes onto your road from a signed snowmobile route on your right. Who must give way?
optionA: You, it comes from the right
optionC: You, as it is off road
explanation: Anyone coming onto a road from a snowmobile route (moottorikelkkailureitti), like from a pihakatu or a path, must always give way to other road users. The right-hand rule does not help it.

question: A car joins your road from a filling station on your left as you approach. Who must give way?
optionB: You, as it is already moving
explanation: Traffic coming from a fuel station, a car park or a yard must give way to traffic on the road, whichever side it comes from.

question: You drive on a road with no signs. A car comes from a side road on your right that looks smaller than yours. Who goes first?
explanation: Without signs or a rule like leaving a car park, the right-hand rule applies at every junction. A wider road gives no priority by itself.

question: Before crossing a level crossing, the barrier starts to move down. What must you do?
optionD: Cross if no train is seen
explanation: Do not start to cross when a train approaches, the signal shows stop, the bell sounds or the barrier is down or moving. Stop at a safe distance.

question: A pedestrian waiting at a zebra crossing waves you through. What should you check before you go?
optionD: That no one else is crossing
explanation: A wave does not clear the crossing for you. Make sure no one else is on or about to step onto it, including in other lanes.

question: You drive past a taajama (built-up area) sign into a village. No speed limit sign follows. What is your limit now?
explanation: The Road Traffic Act sets 50 km/h inside a built-up area and 80 km/h outside one, unless a sign shows a different limit.

question: What is the general speed limit outside built-up areas when no sign shows a limit?
explanation: Outside a built-up area the default limit is 80 km/h. Faster limits, such as on motorways, are always shown by signs.

question: On a two-way road with one lane each way, where should you normally drive?
optionA: In the middle of your lane
optionC: As far right as is safe
explanation: Drive as close to the right edge as safety and other traffic allow. The shoulder is not for normal driving by cars.

question: There are two lanes in your direction on an ordinary road. Which lane should you use?
optionA: The left lane, at all times
explanation: Use the rightmost lane, or another lane where that causes no danger or hindrance. Do not change lanes without need.

question: On a motorway with three lanes in your direction and no queue, which lane should a car use?
optionB: The middle lane, at all times
optionC: The left lane, it is fastest
explanation: On motorways and semi-motorways (moottoriliikennetie) drive in the rightmost free lane unless signs direct lanes to destinations.

question: How may you join a motorway?
optionA: From any lay-by or rest area
optionB: From its start or a slip road
explanation: Vehicles may enter a motorway or semi-motorway only at its start or from an access road, giving way to traffic already on it.

question: Your acceleration lane is ending and traffic on the motorway is dense. What must you not do?
explanation: A driver entering a motorway must give way to vehicles already on it. Use the acceleration lane to match their speed and merge into a gap.

question: You are leaving the motorway at the next exit. What should you do?
optionB: Cut across at the last moment
explanation: Move in good time to the lane nearest the exit and onto the deceleration lane as early as possible.

question: You realise you have just driven past your motorway exit. What is the correct thing to do?
optionA: Drive on to the next exit
optionC: Turn round at the next gap
explanation: Reversing and turning round are forbidden on motorways and semi-motorways. Carry on to the next exit.

question: Which vehicles are not allowed on a motorway?
optionB: Ones limited to 70 km/h or less
explanation: Only motor vehicles may use motorways and semi-motorways, and not those whose maximum permitted or design speed is 70 km/h or less.

question: On a motorway the traffic in every lane is queueing. May you pass a car on its right?
optionA: No, passing on the right is banned
optionB: Only by using the hard shoulder
explanation: In queues, or where lanes are signed for directions, passing on the right without changing lane is allowed on a motorway.

question: May you drive through the crossover between the two carriageways of a motorway?
explanation: Driving on the cross connections between the carriageways of a motorway or semi-motorway is forbidden.

question: You drive through a tunnel marked by a tunnel sign. Which is allowed?
explanation: In a signed tunnel do not reverse or turn back. Stop or park only in an emergency, using the spaces provided, with headlights on.

question: Your car stops for a long time in a signed tunnel because of a queue that is not moving. What should you do?
explanation: If a stop in a tunnel is prolonged, the law requires you to switch off the engine. Keep your headlights on.

question: What is the speed limit in a pihakatu (residential street)?
explanation: In a pihakatu drivers adjust to walking pace and never exceed 20 km/h, giving pedestrians free passage.

question: You drive slowly on a narrow, winding road with a queue behind you. What should you do?
optionA: Keep your speed exactly the same
optionD: Slow down and let them pass
explanation: A much slower vehicle must, when needed, reduce speed and give way to make overtaking easier, and may briefly use the shoulder if safe.

question: Two slow vehicles travel together outside a built-up area. How far apart should they keep?
optionA: Room for a car to cut in
optionB: As close as possible to save room
explanation: Slow motor vehicles outside built-up areas keep gaps that let an overtaking vehicle pull in between them safely.

question: Which is the right way to choose your following distance?
optionB: Enough to avoid a rear-end crash
explanation: The law requires a distance that removes the risk of running into the vehicle in front. Increase it on slippery roads and in poor visibility.

question: May you drive unnecessarily slowly or brake sharply without reason?
optionA: Yes, if the road is empty
explanation: Driving unreasonably slowly and braking suddenly without need are both forbidden, because they cause danger and hold up traffic.

question: You see a sign for a lower winter speed limit on the main road. What does it mean?
optionA: It is only advice for drivers
explanation: Speed limits are lowered on many main roads for winter, and the lower limit on the sign is binding. Adjust further for the actual conditions.

question: A slow van is ahead of you on a two-way road in Finland. On which side do you pass it?
explanation: A vehicle ahead is overtaken on the left. Finland drives on the right.

question: On a two-way road the van ahead slows, moves towards the centre line and signals left. You want to go straight on. What is allowed?
explanation: A vehicle turning left, or clearly getting ready to, may be overtaken only on the right.

question: Your road has two lanes in your direction and both are moving. May you pass a car in the left lane while you stay in the right lane?
explanation: Where there are at least two lanes in your direction and vehicles drive in parallel lanes, passing on the right is allowed.

question: On a one-way street a tram runs down the middle. On which side may you pass it?
explanation: A tram is normally overtaken on the right. On a one-way road, or where the tracks require it, the left is allowed too if it is safe.

question: Where may you not overtake using the oncoming side of the road?
optionC: On a dry road in daylight
explanation: Overtaking at a pedestrian crossing using the oncoming side is forbidden, and so is overtaking in or just before a junction or a level crossing.

question: You are overtaking a lorry when a car behind you flashes its lights to get past. What should you do?
optionA: Brake hard to let it by at once
explanation: Complete your overtake safely and within the limit, then return to the right so faster traffic can pass.

question: Outside a built-up area you approach a junction with no advance sign. May you overtake there?
explanation: The ban on overtaking at junctions does not apply outside built-up areas to junctions that are not shown in advance by a sign.

question: When are you not allowed to overtake using the oncoming lane?
optionA: When the road surface is dry
optionB: When the car ahead is slow
optionD: When a hill blocks the view
explanation: Overtaking on the oncoming side is forbidden if a hill, a bend or anything else limits the view needed to do it safely.

question: You want to overtake, but the driver behind you has already started to overtake you. What do you do?
explanation: You may not overtake on the oncoming side if the vehicle behind has begun overtaking you, or the one ahead is signalling to overtake.

question: The car in front signals that it is about to overtake. May you start overtaking it?
explanation: Overtaking on the oncoming side is not allowed when the vehicle in front shows by signalling that it is about to overtake.

question: You are overtaking, and the car you are passing starts to speed up. What is safest?
optionD: Cut in sharply ahead of it
explanation: If you cannot complete an overtake safely, drop back behind the vehicle. Never race it or cut in.

question: What must an overtaking driver leave between the car and a pedestrian at the roadside?
explanation: The law requires an overtaking driver to keep a safe distance from the vehicle or pedestrian being overtaken. It sets no fixed figure, so give plenty of room.

question: A cyclist is ahead on a narrow village road and a lorry is coming the other way. What should you do?
optionA: Wait until you can give room
explanation: Drivers must give cyclists and pedestrians safe space. If oncoming traffic leaves no room, wait behind the cyclist.

question: Before you return to your lane after overtaking, what must be true?
explanation: Do not overtake on the oncoming side unless you can get back into your lane without danger or seriously hindering others.

question: Road works fill your half of a two-way street and a bus approaches from the front. Who should wait?
explanation: When meeting, the driver on whose side the obstacle is must give way to oncoming traffic.

question: How do you pass an oncoming vehicle on a two-way road?
explanation: Keep to the right when meeting, so the oncoming car passes on your left, driver's side to driver's side. Leave enough room.

question: A traffic island divides a two-way road. On which side do you pass it?
explanation: An island or similar device separating the two directions on a two-way road is passed on the right.

question: When may you sound the horn in normal driving, apart from to avoid danger?
optionA: When the light ahead turns green
optionC: To greet a friend you pass
explanation: The horn is for avoiding danger. Otherwise it may be used only outside built-up areas when overtaking, and never for longer than needed.

question: What signal must you give as you pull out to overtake?
explanation: Changing lane or moving sideways needs a direction signal given in good time and kept on for the whole manoeuvre.

question: Which may you use for a short time to help a faster car overtake you?
optionB: The pavement, if it is empty
optionD: The shoulder, if it is safe
explanation: A slow driver letting others pass may drive briefly on the shoulder if it does not endanger safety or hold up other traffic.

question: You approach a level crossing behind a slow van. May you overtake it just before the crossing?
optionB: Yes, if no train is near
explanation: Overtaking in or immediately before a level crossing is forbidden.

question: What should you check before pulling out to overtake?
optionA: Only the road ahead of you
optionB: Mirrors, blind spot and road ahead
explanation: Check behind, including the blind spot, and make sure the oncoming lane is clear far enough ahead before you start.

question: In a built-up area a junction lies just ahead. May you overtake right before it?
optionD: Only if no sign is there
explanation: Overtaking in a junction or immediately before one is forbidden. Outside built-up areas the ban covers junctions shown by an advance sign.

question: On a road with one lane each way, which side may you use to overtake?
optionA: The hard shoulder, if it is wide
explanation: Where there is only one lane in your direction, you may use the oncoming side to overtake, if it is clear and no ban applies.

question: How close to a pedestrian crossing may you stop or park in front of it?
explanation: Stopping and parking are forbidden on a crossing and within 5 metres before it, so drivers can see people stepping out.

question: Near a junction, where does the ban on stopping and parking apply?
explanation: Do not stop or park in a junction or closer than 5 metres to the nearest edge of the crossing carriageway.

question: You want to leave your car near a railway level crossing. How far from it must you park?
explanation: Parking within 30 metres of a railway level crossing is forbidden, in addition to the general stopping bans.

question: On which side of a two-way road outside a built-up area must you stop or park?
explanation: Stop or park only on the right side of the road. The left side is allowed on one-way roads, and in built-up areas on two-way roads if it causes no danger or hindrance.

question: In a built-up area, may you park on the left side of a two-way street?
explanation: In built-up areas stopping and parking on the left side of a two-way road is allowed if it does not endanger or hinder traffic.

question: How should a parked car be placed on the street?
optionA: At an angle to the kerb
optionB: Parallel and close to the edge
optionD: In the middle of the lane, angled
explanation: A stopped or parked vehicle must be parallel to the road and as close to its edge as possible, unless markings show otherwise.

question: May you park on a priority road outside a built-up area?
optionA: Yes, if you switch on hazards
explanation: Parking on the carriageway of a road signed as a priority road is forbidden outside built-up areas.

question: A solid line runs along the road. How much room must be left between your parked car and the line?
explanation: Do not stop or park beside a solid line if less than 3 metres would remain between your car and the line, unless a broken line runs between them.

question: Where is stopping forbidden?
explanation: Stopping and parking are forbidden in a roundabout, on cycle and bus lanes, in underpasses, tunnels, on crests and on blind bends.

question: May you park next to a car that is already parked along the kerb?
optionC: Yes, with the driver inside it
explanation: Parking alongside another vehicle parked at the edge is forbidden, unless that vehicle is a two-wheeled bicycle or moped.

question: A parking sign limits parking time and requires the start time to be shown. What may you mark as the start time?
optionA: Any time you choose to write
optionB: The time you plan to leave
optionC: The next full or half hour
explanation: Mark the time you parked. You may instead mark the next full or half hour after it, whichever of the two comes sooner. Do not change it while parked.

question: May you briefly stop a car on a pavement to unload heavy goods?
optionC: Yes, for up to an hour
optionD: Only if no other place exists
explanation: A car may stop on a pavement or cycle path for a short time to load or unload only with compelling reasons and no other place nearby. The driver stays close.

question: Where would stopping your car break the law?
explanation: Stopping and parking on a cycle lane or a bus lane is forbidden.

question: When is stopping in a no-stopping place allowed?
optionA: To check a message on your phone
optionB: To give way or in an emergency
explanation: Even where stopping is banned, you may stop because of an unavoidable obstruction, to give way, or in an emergency.

question: Where may you park on a pihakatu (residential street)?
explanation: Parking in a pihakatu is allowed only at marked parking places, apart from bicycles, mopeds and cars with a disabled or home care permit.

question: Where may you park on a motorway?
optionA: On the hard shoulder, with hazards
explanation: On motorways and semi-motorways stopping and parking are allowed only at signed parking places, service and rest areas, or at a signed bus stop.

question: You leave your car at the roadside. What must you make sure of?
explanation: The driver must make sure a stopped or parked vehicle cannot start moving uncontrolled: use the parking brake and a gear.

question: What does the Road Traffic Act say about opening a parked car's doors and unloading it?
optionA: Only the driver's door is covered
optionB: It must not endanger or hinder others
optionC: It applies only in built-up areas
explanation: Doors must not be opened, people must not get in or out, and a vehicle must not be loaded or unloaded in a way that endangers or hinders other traffic, including cyclists.

question: May you park a car you no longer use on the street for months?
optionA: Yes, as long as it is insured
optionB: Yes, in a quiet side street
optionC: No, storage on roads is banned
optionD: Yes, with a cover on it
explanation: A vehicle that is not actually used in traffic must not be left or stored on the road.

question: You park on an unlit road in the dark, outside a car park. What lights does the car need?
optionA: No lights, as it is parked
explanation: A car stopped or parked on the road in darkness needs front position lights or dipped lights, and rear lights, unless the road is lit well enough for it to be seen. In a built-up area a parking light may be used instead when parked parallel to the road.

question: Most European warning triangles have a white background. Finnish warning triangles instead have:
explanation: Finnish warning signs are triangles with a yellow background and a red border, unlike the white ones used in most of Europe.

question: What do Finnish prohibition and restriction signs, such as a speed limit, usually look like?
explanation: Prohibition and restriction signs are round with a red border. In Finland most have a yellow background, including speed limit signs.

question: At the end of a street in Oulu, a round blue sign shows a white arrow curving to the right. Which way may you go?
explanation: Blue circles are mandatory signs. A white arrow orders you to go in its direction only.

question: A sign under a warning triangle has a yellow background and a red border. What is it?
explanation: Additional panels under warning, priority and prohibition signs have a yellow background, a red border and usually black text or symbols.

question: A yellow triangle shows a moose. When is the risk of meeting one highest?
optionA: At dusk and in the dark
explanation: Moose and deer warning signs mark stretches where elk often cross. The risk is highest at dusk, at dawn and in the dark, especially in autumn.

question: A warning sign shows a reindeer. What should you expect?
explanation: Reindeer roam freely in the reindeer herding area in the north and may stand on the road. Slow down and be ready to stop.

question: A sign shows a yellow diamond with a white border crossed by a diagonal band. What does it mean?
explanation: The yellow diamond marks a priority road; the same sign crossed by a band marks its end, after which normal rules apply again.

question: A downward-pointing triangle with a red border stands at your side of a junction. What must you do?
optionC: Give way only to the right
explanation: This is the give-way sign. You must let traffic on the crossing road go first, stopping if necessary.

question: A red octagon reading STOP stands at the junction, but the crossing road looks empty. What must you do?
explanation: The stop sign requires a full stop before the stop line or the junction every time, then giving way to traffic on the crossing road.

question: Which sign tells you to give way to oncoming traffic at a narrow passage?
explanation: The give-way-to-oncoming sign is round with a red border and two opposing arrows. Oncoming drivers see the blue square sign that gives them priority.

question: Before a narrow bridge you see a blue square sign on which your white arrow is larger than the red one. An oncoming car is still far off. What do you do?
optionD: Cross only at walking pace, slowly
explanation: This sign gives you priority over oncoming traffic on the narrow stretch. Oncoming drivers face the opposite sign and must wait.

question: A yellow warning triangle shows only a black exclamation mark, with a panel below it. What does it warn of?
optionD: A danger named on the panel
explanation: The exclamation mark means a danger that has no sign of its own. The additional panel below, yellow with a red border, usually says what it is, such as a ferry berth or frost damage.

question: A round sign with a red border shows the number 60. What does it mean?
explanation: A number in a prohibition circle is a speed limit. It applies until the next junction or a sign that ends or changes it.

question: A rectangular sign shows a speed limit in a circle with the word for zone. What does it mean?
optionB: The limit covers the whole area
explanation: A speed limit zone sign sets the limit for every road in the area until a sign shows the zone has ended.

question: A sign shows a silhouette of buildings at the edge of town. What does it mark?
explanation: This sign marks the start of a taajama (built-up area). Unless a sign shows otherwise, the limit inside is 50 km/h.

question: A blue sign shows a house, a child playing and a car. What does it mark?
optionA: A car park for a playground
explanation: In a pihakatu pedestrians may use the whole street, drivers give them free passage and keep to 20 km/h or less.

question: A blue sign shows walking people only. What may you do with a car there?
optionA: Reach a property with no other access
optionB: Drive through it at walking pace
optionC: Park on it for up to an hour
optionD: Use it as a short cut
explanation: On a kävelykatu (pedestrian street) a motor vehicle may drive only to a property with no other access, or for servicing if a sign allows it, at 20 km/h or less.

question: Near a school in Espoo, a blue square sign with a white triangle and a walking figure stands beside the road. How should you approach?
optionA: At the same speed as before
explanation: This sign marks a pedestrian crossing. Approach at a speed that lets you stop for anyone on it or about to step onto it.

question: You stop under a no-parking sign, a red circle with one diagonal bar. What may you do there?
optionA: Leave the car for ten minutes
optionD: Nothing, even a stop is banned
explanation: One diagonal bar means no parking; two crossed bars mean no stopping. Short stops to pick up or drop passengers are allowed under a no parking sign.

question: A round sign with a red border has two red bars crossing in an X. What does it mean?
explanation: The crossed bars forbid stopping as well as parking, except where traffic or an emergency forces you to stop.

question: A red circle with a white horizontal bar faces you at the start of a street. What does it mean?
explanation: This is the no-entry sign, usually seen at the exit end of a one-way street. Do not drive in.

question: A blue P sign in a shopping street has a plate below showing a parking disc and 2 h. What does it mean?
optionB: Park up to 2 h, using a disc
explanation: The P sign marks a parking place. A plate with a parking disc symbol and a time limits how long you may park, and you must set your parking disc.

question: A yellow triangle shows a car whose wheels leave wavy tracks. What is the hazard?
explanation: This sign warns that the surface may be slippery. Slow down, avoid sudden braking or steering and increase your distance.

question: You pass a road works warning sign and a lower speed limit on a Sunday, but nobody is working. What applies?
optionD: The signs and limit still apply
explanation: Temporary signs and limits at a work site are binding while they stand, even when no one is working: the road may be uneven, narrowed or have loose gravel. Follow them and any yellow markings.

question: On a country road you see a yellow triangle with a steam locomotive in it. What lies ahead?
explanation: A locomotive shows a level crossing without barriers. A fence symbol is used for a crossing with barriers.

question: A warning sign shows a tram. What should you expect?
optionB: Trams crossing or sharing the road
optionC: A tram stop only, no tracks
explanation: This sign warns of a tram line crossing or running along the road. Remember that trams generally have priority.

question: You are overtaking on a divided road when you pass a yellow triangle with one arrow up and one arrow down. What should you do?
explanation: The sign means the divided road ends and oncoming traffic will soon use the other lane. Complete or abandon the overtake and return to the right in good time.

question: A warning triangle shows a cyclist. What should you do?
explanation: This sign warns that a cycle path crosses or joins the road, or that many cyclists use it. Slow down and look out for them.

question: A yellow triangle warns of a roundabout ahead. What will you usually find at its entry?
explanation: This sign warns of a roundabout. Slow down and expect a give-way sign at its entry: traffic on the ring goes first.

question: Some electronic signs show a white symbol on a black background. Are they valid?
explanation: On variable signs the symbol may be light on a black background. They have the same force as fixed signs.

question: A sign marks a pyöräkatu (bicycle street). How should you drive there?
explanation: On a signed pyöräkatu (bicycle street) drivers give cyclists free passage and adjust their speed to cycling.

question: At a Finnish level crossing without barriers, red lights flash but the track looks empty both ways. May you cross?
optionC: Yes, if you sound the horn
explanation: Flashing red lights at a level crossing mean a train is coming. Stop at a safe distance and do not cross until they stop.

question: You see a continuous yellow line along the middle of a Finnish road. What does its colour tell you?
explanation: Finland marks the lines between opposite traffic flows in yellow. White lines separate lanes going the same way and mark edges.

question: What does a continuous line in the middle of the road mean?
optionB: Do not cross or drive on it
explanation: A continuous line (sulkuviiva) must not be crossed or straddled. It is often used where overtaking would be dangerous.

question: The dashes of the centre line become much longer and the gaps shorter. What is this telling you?
optionA: A bus stop on the right ahead
optionC: A solid line or danger ahead
explanation: A warning line has longer dashes and shorter gaps than a normal centre line. It tells you a continuous line or a risky stretch is coming.

question: There is a continuous line on your side and a broken line on the other side of it. May you cross?
explanation: With a double line you may cross only from the side with the broken line. A continuous line on your side means you stay in your lane.

question: A STOP sign and a stop line stand before a railway level crossing with no barriers. What must you do?
optionA: Stop at the line and look
optionC: Stop only if a train shows
explanation: At a STOP sign you must stop at the stop line every time, then cross only when you have made sure no train is coming.

question: A row of white triangles across your lane marks a give-way line. If you must stop, where do you stop?
explanation: The triangles, known as shark's teeth, mark where you must give way. If you need to stop, stop before them.

question: Lane arrows show your lane turns left only, but you want to go straight. What should you do?
explanation: Once in a lane marked by arrows you must follow them. Choose the right lane in good time; if you are wrong, follow the arrow and find a new route.

question: Both the red and the yellow lights are on at once. What happens next?
explanation: Red and yellow together mean the light is about to turn green. Get ready, but do not move off until green shows.

question: The light turns yellow when you are a few metres from the stop line, too close to stop without braking hard. What should you do?
optionB: Brake hard to stop at once
explanation: Yellow means stop before the stop line, unless you are so close that you could not stop safely.

question: Late at night the lights at a junction flash yellow, and a give-way sign stands on your side. Who goes first?
optionA: You, the light is not red
explanation: Flashing yellow means the lights are not controlling traffic, only warning. The signs and the general rules apply, so the give-way sign decides.

question: A separate green arrow for turning right goes dark while the round light stays red. What does that mean?
explanation: A green arrow lets traffic go in its direction only while it is lit. When it goes out, the round red light applies to you.

question: Lights are mounted over each lane of a road. Which light applies to you?
optionA: The one on the right-hand side
explanation: When signals are placed lane by lane above the road, each light applies only to vehicles using that lane.

question: A pedestrian crosses at lights with a pedestrian signal. Which light must they follow?
explanation: Pedestrians follow pedestrian signals first, and the vehicle lights for their direction only where there is no pedestrian signal.

question: A police officer stands with one arm raised straight up. What does it mean?
optionC: Speed up and clear the junction
explanation: An arm raised straight up means stop for all approaching traffic, except drivers who could no longer stop safely.

question: A police officer faces you with an arm stretched out to the side. What should you do?
explanation: Traffic facing the front or back of an officer with arms stretched sideways must stop. Traffic moving parallel to the arms may go.

question: Which take priority over all other traffic controls?
explanation: A road user must follow signs, orders and bans given by a traffic controller first, even if they differ from lights, signs or markings.

question: You pass a tram at a stop on its right. Passengers are getting off. What must you do?
explanation: When passing a tram or bus on its right at a stop, give unobstructed passage to passengers getting on or off.

question: Where should a pedestrian walk on a road with no pavement or shoulder?
explanation: On the carriageway a pedestrian uses the left edge, facing traffic, unless the right side is safer. Someone pushing a bicycle may use the right.

question: A pedestrian in dark clothes walks on an unlit road at night. What should they normally use?
explanation: The law says pedestrians should generally use a reflector when moving in the dark. Dipped headlights reveal an unlit pedestrian very late.

question: Which children may cycle on the pavement in Finland?
explanation: A child under 12 may cycle on the pavement if it does not seriously hinder pedestrians.

question: What is the minimum age to ride an electric scooter or other light electric vehicle?
explanation: The rider of a light electric vehicle, such as a rental e-scooter, must be at least 15.

question: A cyclist ahead wants to turn left at a junction. What may the cyclist do instead of moving to the centre?
optionA: Turn left from the right edge at once
optionB: Cross on the right side, then turn
explanation: A cyclist turning left may continue across the crossing road along the right side and then turn, once it can be done safely.

question: You approach a stopped school bus with children around it. What should you do?
optionC: Slow down, be ready to stop
explanation: Take special care near a stopped school or day care transport, a bus or a tram, and near children, elderly people or anyone who struggles in traffic.

question: An elderly person is crossing slowly where there is no crossing. What should you do?
optionA: Sound the horn to hurry them
explanation: Drivers must give pedestrians safe space and take special care near people who have clear difficulty coping in traffic.

question: A child runs onto the road after a ball. What is the right lesson for your driving?
optionD: Use the horn constantly near parks
explanation: Children can act suddenly. Near schools, play areas and homes, slow down and be ready to stop.

question: Outside built-up areas, where does a moped normally ride?
optionA: In the middle of the lane
optionB: On the shoulder or road edge
explanation: Outside built-up areas a moped rides on the shoulder or at the edge of the carriageway when this can be done without hindrance.

question: You turn right across a cycle path running beside the road. A cyclist approaches on it. Who goes first?
explanation: A turning driver gives way to cyclists and moped riders crossing the road being entered, and anyone on a cycle path or pavement being crossed.

question: A horse rider is ahead on a narrow road. How should you pass?
optionA: Quickly, to get it over with
explanation: Give animals and their riders safe space and pass slowly. A frightened horse can move into your path.

question: Who may use the whole width of a pihakatu, including the carriageway?
explanation: In a pihakatu and a kävelykatu pedestrians may walk on all parts of the street, though they must not hold up vehicles needlessly.

question: A dog is being walked along the road. What does the law expect of its owner?
optionA: Let it run free beside them
explanation: An animal on the road must be leashed or supervised so it causes no danger, and kept as close to the road edge as possible.

question: What applies to an electric scooter rider on the road?
explanation: Riders of light electric vehicles and motor-assisted bicycles follow the traffic rules and signs that apply to cyclists.

question: What is the maximum speed of a rental e-scooter with its motor helping?
explanation: A light electric vehicle, an e-bike or a motor-assisted bicycle may go at most 25 km/h when the motor is used to keep up speed.

question: A pedestrian is walking towards you at the edge of a narrow road at night. What should you do?
optionB: Use full beam to see them
explanation: Use dipped headlights so you do not dazzle, slow down and leave a wide gap. Pedestrians in the dark are seen very late.

question: You approach a pedestrian crossing where your view is blocked by a parked van. What should you do?
optionB: Slow down, be ready to stop
explanation: If the view of a crossing is limited, slow down and stop if needed before it. Someone may be stepping out behind the van.

question: You approach a pedestrian crossing. What speed should you keep?
optionC: One that lets you stop before it
explanation: The law requires special care and a speed at which you could stop before the crossing if needed.

question: Your car is in a queue that stops on a pedestrian crossing. What should you have done?
optionA: Moved right up to the car ahead
explanation: Plan ahead so you do not stop on a crossing or in a junction. Wait until there is room beyond it.

question: Under the Finnish Criminal Code, from what blood alcohol level is driving a car drink driving?
explanation: Drink driving starts at 0.5 per mille in the blood or 0.22 mg per litre of exhaled breath. Finland has no lower limit for new drivers, so the safe amount is none.

question: What breath alcohol level is the drink driving limit in Finland?
explanation: The breath limit is 0.22 mg of alcohol per litre of exhaled air, matching 0.5 per mille in the blood.

question: From what blood alcohol level is drink driving aggravated?
explanation: Aggravated drink driving starts at 1.2 per mille in the blood or 0.53 mg per litre of breath, or when driving ability is clearly impaired.

question: You were at a party until late and drank a lot. What is true when you wake up?
optionD: You may still be over the limit
explanation: The body removes alcohol slowly, and nothing speeds it up. After a heavy evening you may still be over the limit the next morning.

question: Your phone rings while you drive in Helsinki. Which way of answering is allowed?
optionD: On speaker, held in your hand
explanation: A driver of a motor vehicle may not use a communication device while holding it in the hand. Even hands-free use must not distract you.

question: You feel very sleepy on a long drive. What is the safest action?
explanation: No one may drive when tired, ill or impaired. Fresh air and music do not cure sleepiness; only rest does.

question: Which medicine warning should make you think twice about driving?
optionA: A green leaf on the package
optionC: A red triangle on the pack
explanation: In Finland a red warning triangle on a medicine pack means it can affect your ability to drive. Ask a pharmacist or doctor.

question: You arrive first at a crash where people are hurt. What does the law require?
optionA: Drive on to find the police
optionD: Stay and help as you can
explanation: A road user must stay at the scene of a road accident, help the injured as far as able and take part in the necessary measures. Call 112.

question: At what age can you normally get a category B licence in Finland?
explanation: The age for category B is 18. With an age exception permit, a driving licence can be granted from 17.

question: Since 29 May 2026, what applies to every 17-year-old driving a car on an age exception licence?
optionB: No driving from midnight to 5 a.m.
explanation: The amended Driving Licence Act bans all 17-year-olds from driving a category B vehicle between 00.00 and 05.00, including those who got their licence before 29 May 2026.

question: From 1 October 2026, what must a 17-year-old driving a car display?
optionA: An L plate on the rear
explanation: From 1 October 2026 a sign identifying an underage driver is mandatory for all 17-year-olds driving passenger cars.

question: How long is a passed theory test valid for booking the driving test?
explanation: A passed theory test is valid for one year. Take the driving test within that time or you must pass the theory test again.

question: What happens if you cheat in the theory test?
explanation: Cheating in the theory test, including copying or recording it, leads to a six-month ban from taking the test.

question: How many parts does the category B theory test have?
explanation: The test has verbal multiple choice questions, picture questions about traffic situations and risk recognition questions. You must pass each part.

question: In the category B theory test, how many of the 50 traffic picture questions must you answer correctly?
explanation: Traficom requires at least 43 of the 50 picture questions, 11 of the 15 multiple choice questions and 4 of the 5 risk recognition questions.

question: What time limit does the standard tablet theory test have?
explanation: The standard theory test is taken on a tablet with 30 minutes to answer. An oral test with 60 minutes is allowed in certain cases.

question: In which languages is the Finnish theory test offered?
explanation: Traficom gives Finnish, Swedish and English as the languages of the test. An interpreter may be allowed in an oral test in some cases.

question: How early may you take the theory test for a car licence?
optionA: Six months before the licence age
optionB: One month before the licence age
optionD: One week before the licence age
explanation: Traficom allows the theory test one month before you reach the age requirement for the licence: one month before 18, or one month before 17 with an age exception permit.

question: What should a driver do about a passenger who distracts them on a busy road?
explanation: The driver is responsible for keeping full attention on traffic. Ask passengers not to distract you, and stop if needed.

question: How does a driver best anticipate traffic, as the law requires?
optionA: Watch only the car in front
optionB: Rely on your right of way
explanation: Road users must anticipate others' actions to avoid danger. Scan far ahead and be ready for others to make mistakes.

question: In which months must a car have winter tyres if the weather or road conditions require them?
explanation: The Road Traffic Act requires winter tyres in November, December, January, February and March when the weather or road conditions require them.

question: When winter tyres are required, how deep must their main grooves be at least?
explanation: Winter tyres on a car must have at least 3.0 mm of tread in the main grooves. Summer tyres need at least 1.6 mm.

question: Under Finnish law, what tread depth must a car's summer tyres have at least?
explanation: Car tyres need at least 1.6 mm in the main grooves. Much more is needed for good grip on wet roads.

question: When may studded tyres normally be used on a car?
explanation: Studded tyres are allowed from the start of November to the end of March, and at other times if the weather or road conditions require them.

question: If you fit studded tyres to a car, where must they go?
explanation: Studded tyres on a car must be fitted to all wheels, so the car grips evenly front and rear.

question: Which lights must a car use while driving in daylight?
explanation: A motor vehicle must always use headlights or daytime running lights while driving. In darkness, at dusk or in poor visibility, headlights and rear lights are required.

question: Where is full beam not allowed?
optionB: On a country road at night
explanation: Do not use full beam on a lit road, when it could dazzle an oncoming driver, or when driving close behind another vehicle.

question: In which conditions is the rear fog light allowed?
explanation: Front and rear fog lights may be used in fog or heavy rain. The rear one also when spray or snow raised by traffic hides the car from behind.

question: How long may an engine idle when a car is parked in normal weather?
explanation: A combustion engine may not idle for more than two minutes when the vehicle stands for a reason other than a traffic stop.

question: It is colder than minus 15 °C. How long may you idle the engine before setting off?
explanation: In frost of more than 15 °C the engine may run for up to four minutes before driving off. Use an engine heater to warm it instead.

question: You tow a broken-down car with a rope. How far apart must the cars be?
explanation: With a towing rope the gap between vehicles must be at least 3 and at most 6 metres. A car with faulty brakes may be towed only with a rigid bar.

question: What is the maximum speed when towing a car on its own wheels?
explanation: When a motor vehicle is towed on its own wheels the limit is 60 km/h, unless a lower one applies to either vehicle.

question: Your car breaks down on the carriageway outside a built-up area where others may not see it in time. What must you do?
optionB: Leave it and walk for help
explanation: The driver must set out the warning triangle far enough back for others to notice in good time, and take other warning steps if needed.

question: In which situation are hazard warning lights allowed?
optionA: When parked illegally for a minute
optionB: When stopped where it is dangerous
explanation: Hazard lights may be used on a vehicle stopped after an accident or breakdown where it endangers others, and while moving to warn of an immediate danger.

question: A 5-year-old shorter than 135 cm takes a taxi that has no child seat. How may the child travel?
optionA: On an adult's lap in front
optionB: Without any belt in the back
optionC: With a seat belt, not in front
explanation: A taxi without a child restraint may carry a child under 135 cm using a seat belt in a seat other than a front seat. A child under 3 may never travel without a child restraint.

question: Below what height must a child in a car use a child restraint?
explanation: A child shorter than 135 cm must use a child restraint in a car, van or lorry with seat belts. A child under 3 may never travel without one.

question: Your number plate is covered in snow and road dirt. What must you do?
explanation: Number plates must be clean and readable. Clear snow and dirt from them, and from the lights, before you set off.

question: You hit a moose and it runs into the forest. What should you do?
optionA: Drive on if the car works
explanation: Report a collision with a large animal at once through the emergency number 112, even if it ran off. Mark the place so it can be traced.

question: What is the main reason to warm the engine with a heater on frosty mornings?
optionD: It lets you skip winter tyres
explanation: An engine heater makes cold starts easier, cuts emissions and wear, and replaces long idling, which the law limits.

question: On a frosty Lapland morning you have scraped a small hole in the windscreen only. Is that enough to drive off?
explanation: You must be able to see and be seen. Clear snow and ice from all windows, mirrors, lights and the roof before you drive.
